name: Englebright Dam
scope: Complete surviving Englebright concrete arch dam: curved ungated ogee overflow crest and tapered downstream/upstream walls, intrinsic raised nonoverflow end/abutment wings, four main tall intermediate crest piers/low end transitions and own maintenance rails/representative construction joints. Static dry structural exterior only; four tall interior piers divide five visibly overflowing central bays in the2010photo. No moving gates, low-level outlet, modeled water/spray/rainbow, adjacent Narrows I/II powerhouses/intakes, river/rock/forest/boats/roads or landscape. Original native NHD dam polygon identifies approximate curved envelope; exact crest/footing/abutment sections and hidden foundations are not surveyed.
era: Surviving1941concrete arch dam, Qualla-published USACE aerial and Michael J. NevinsJune2010spillway photograph. Represent dry concrete structure, not date-specific overflowing water or temporary maintenance.

references.caption: Englebright Dam, shown here June 10, 2010, is located between Grass Valley and Marysville, Calif., in Nevada and Yuba counties. Completed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District in 1941, the dam was authorized by Congress for the storage of hydraulic gold mining debris on the Yuba River.  The concrete arch dam spans 1,142 feet across and is 260 feet high. Englebright Lake is 9 miles long with a surface area of 815 acres, an elevation of 527 feet and 24 miles of shoreline. The lake and dam are managed by the Sacramento District. (U.S. Army Photo/ Michael  J. Nevins)

candidates.filename: Building a 3-D model of Yuba River canyon (6649701211).jpg
candidates.caption: Rocko Brown, a doctoral candidate in geomorphology at the University of California-Davis, photographs the Yuba River canyon below Englebright Dam near Smartsville, Calif., Jan. 6, 2012. Researchers at the University of California-Davis will use the images to create a virtual 3-D model of the river canyon to aid future research. Under the direction of the National Marine Fisheries Service, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District, which owns and manages the dam, has placed more than 5,000 tons of gravel in the river to improve spawning habitat for the threatened Chinook salmon and steelhead trout species. Dr. Greg Pasternack, hydrology professor at UC-Davis, designed the gravel injection project and is evaluating the gravel’s movement through the river course. (U.S. Army photo by Chris Gray-Garcia/Released)

candidates.filename: Corps reconnaissance team tours Yuba River (14437959656).jpg
candidates.caption: Yuba River water emerges from one of the two power-generating structures immediately downstream of Englebright Dam. Members of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District team assessing possible federal projects for ecosystem restoration along Northern California's Yuba River reviewed the water’s route from Daguerre Point Dam up to Downieville on a site visit June 18, 2014. The Corps team was accompanied by members of the Yuba County Water Agency and several YCWA consultants in this initial trip to gather data on the overall state of the Yuba and water facilities along the route. (U.S. Army photo by Robert Kidd / Released)

candidates.filename: Yuba River below Englebright dam USACE.jpg
candidates.caption:
CALIFORNIA — Rocko Brown, a doctoral candidate in geomorphology at the University of California-Davis, photographs the Yuba River Canyon, below Englebright Dam near Smartsville, Yuba County, California (Jan. 6, 2012). 
Researchers at the University of California-Davis will use the images to create a virtual 3D model of the river canyon to aid future research.
Under the direction of the National Marine Fisheries Service, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Sacramento District, which owns and manages the dam, has placed more than 5,000 tons of gravel in the river to improve spawning habitat for the threatened Chinook salmon (Oncorhynchus tshawytscha) and Steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) species.
Dr. Greg Pasternack, professor of land, air and water resources at UC-Davis, designed the gravel injection project and is evaluating the gravel’s movement through the river course. (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers photo by Chris Gray-Garcia)

candidates.caption: Map of the watershed of the Yuba River in Nevada and Yuba Counties, California, USA. Map drawn by the U.S. Geological Service (USGS) for bathymetric and geophysical surveys of Englebright Lake, which is impounded by Englebright Dam on the Yuba River. The black borders encompass the entire watershed of the three forks of the Yuba River. The green borders encompass the limits of the USGS Upper Yuba River Watershed Studies Program (UYRSP) area. Map slightly reworked by contributor from source map and converted to PNG.
